issues.legal_issue: Whether a resolution and an acceptance document together created a lease whose lack of registration affected the parties’ rights.
material_facts: No lease was executed in furtherance of the property authority’s resolution.
The claimants relied on the resolution together with the occupants’ acceptance document as creating a lease.
The dispute reached the Court on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The resolution and acceptance document did not together create a lease, so the question of the legal effect of an unregistered lease did not arise.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not decide the general question whether an unregistered lease requiring compulsory registration can confer legal rights, because it found that no lease was created by the documents in this case. It noted that the general question was settled by a long course of decisions but cited no particular provision or earlier case.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The parties brought an appeal concerning a claimed right to remain in possession of property.
predicates.no_separate_lease_executed: No lease document was executed to implement the property authority’s resolution.
predicates.claim_based_on_combined_documents: The claimants relied on a property authority’s resolution and the occupants’ acceptance document together as constituting a lease.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a claimed right based on combined documents, and no separate lease was executed, the rule means those documents do not create a lease.

issues.legal_issue: Whether an arrangement permitting possession for one year at a time, with an annual payment and an option to continue, was a year-to-year tenancy or a lease reserving yearly rent.
material_facts: Under the arrangement, the occupants were entitled to remain in possession for one year at a time.
They could pay the rent for the whole year in one lump sum.
At the end of each year, they were entitled to continue in possession for another year, and so on.
The Court considered the lower courts’ characterization of the arrangement on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The arrangement permitted possession for one year at a time, subject to the right to continue for another year at the end of each year; it was not a year-to-year tenancy or a lease reserving yearly rent.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the annual lump-sum payment and the right to continue for successive one-year periods as facilities available to the occupants, not as making the arrangement a year-to-year tenancy or a lease reserving yearly rent. No statutory provision or particular earlier case was cited for this characterization.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and possession_granted_one_year_at_a_time and annual_lump_sum_payment_allowed and annual_continuation_right

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The parties brought an appeal concerning the characterization of an arrangement for possession of property.
predicates.possession_granted_one_year_at_a_time: The property authority’s arrangement allowed the occupants to remain in possession for one year at a time.
predicates.annual_lump_sum_payment_allowed: The arrangement allowed the occupants to pay the rent for a whole year in one lump sum.
predicates.annual_continuation_right: The arrangement entitled the occupants to continue in possession for another year at the end of each year.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an arrangement allowing possession one year at a time, annual lump-sum payment, and continuation for another year at each year’s end, the rule means the occupancy is not a year-to-year tenancy.
